description: We are high school students and we are trying NASA Space Apps Challenge for the very first time, and we are looking to broaden our understanding about the Earth.
summary: Earth Jukebox translates NASA Earth science imagery into dynamic soundscapes to make complex climate and ocean data accessible to everyone. Using NASA’s Perpetual Ocean 2 visualization (ECCO2 model, SVS ID: 5425), our project transforms swirling deep-water ocean currents off the eastern coast of North America into an immersive auditory experience. By capturing visual frames and mapping the vertical position and brightness of the cyan current trails to musical pitch and audio intensity, listeners can hear the hidden motion of deep-water countercurrents beneath the ocean surface. Pairing sight with sound allows blind, low-vision, and auditory learners to experience how our oceans move and change, bridging the accessibility gap in traditional visual-only science communication.
details:
What It Does:
Earth Jukebox pairs NASA Earth Information Center (EIC) visualizations with custom-generated soundscapes so users can experience planetary data through both sight and sound. Our project sonifies deep ocean currents flowing more than 600 meters below the surface in the Gulf Stream region off the eastern coast of North America.

How We Built It:
We extracted a visual frame from NASA’s Perpetual Ocean 2 (ECCO2 model) visualization and processed it through an image-to-sound sonification tool. As the tool scans across the imagery, the vertical position and brightness of the swirling blue and cyan current trails dynamically control the pitch and intensity of the generated audio. Finally, we paired the resulting soundscape directly with the NASA visualization video so audiences can watch and listen to the ocean patterns simultaneously.
Why It Matters & Impact:
Vital Earth science data is often shared exclusively through visuals, which limits access for blind and low-vision communities. By translating visual flow patterns into sound, Earth Jukebox creates an inclusive, multi-sensory way for learners of all abilities to explore and connect with our planet.

Project Creative: Most people only get to look at NASA ocean maps, so we wanted to figure out a way for people to actually hear them instead. We took a frame of deep-water currents from NASA’s Perpetual Ocean 2 visualization and used an image-to-sound tool so the brightness and height of the swirling currents control the pitch and volume of the audio. Pairing that sound directly with the video lets people experience hidden ocean movement in a new way that doesn't rely just on sight.

Factors Considered: We wanted to make sure our project was accessible for blind and low-vision learners who usually get left out when science is only shown through charts and videos. We also paid close attention to making the audio match what was happening on screen, so brighter and higher currents sounded noticeably different instead of just playing random audio. Finally, we kept our layout simple so anyone can just hit play and immediately hear and see how the deep ocean currents move.
